description: verification-architecture.md's NFR-6/PROP-049 description claims 'every test constructs its client with an injected fetchImpl/execFileImpl/walletClientFactory (never globalThis.fetch/a bare createRealXxx() with no transport override)', but the ACTUAL PROP-049 scan (lib/real-clients/__tests__/test-money-safety-scan.test.mjs) only greps for real-endpoint URL literals in source text -- it never checks for the presence/absence of an injected transport override. In practice, two tests in base-signer.test.mjs (PROP-041's 'getAddress throws when ANICCA_HOME is unset' and PROP-042's 'getAddress returns the address...') construct `createRealBaseSigner({ env: {...} })` with NO fetchImpl override at all. This happens to be safe (getAddress() never reaches the network in this implementation), but the written verification-architecture claim overclaims what the automated scan actually enforces, and nothing would catch a FUTURE test that added a bare createRealXxx() call on a code path that DOES reach the network.
